faqs.question: How do I receive payment in Liberia as a freelancer?
faqs.answer: The proven setup is Payoneer for Upwork and Fiverr payouts, plus Wise for direct client bank transfers with low fees, and then withdrawing to your Liberian bank account or mobile money such as Orange Money or MTN MoMo. We show you how to open and verify each account early so your payments are never held up.

faqs.question: Do I need experience or a university degree to start freelancing?
faqs.answer: No. Many successful freelancers start with no experience and no degree. This course shows you how to identify a skill you already have, create sample work to prove it, and win your first clients through strong profiles and personalized proposals.

faqs.question: How do I deal with unreliable internet and electricity in Liberia?
faqs.answer: We teach practical planning: buy data bundles ahead of deadlines, keep a power bank or generator backup, and deliver work early so an outage never causes a late delivery. Fiverr gigs are also ideal because orders arrive even when you are offline.

faqs.question: Is this course really free and is the certificate recognized?
faqs.answer: Yes, it is completely free with no credit card required. On passing the final assessment you receive a TIH certificate with a unique verification code that employers and clients can confirm as genuine.

🧭 What is Remote Work?

This lesson explains What is Remote Work? so you can understand remote employment, freelancing, opportunities, challenges, and professional responsibility. It joins client need, proof, agreement, execution, trust, and improvement.

Definition

Remote work is an employment or service arrangement in which work is performed outside a traditional shared workplace and coordinated through agreed digital systems, schedules, outputs, and policies.

🔑 Key Words & Meanings

What is Remote Work?

paid work performed away from a traditional shared office using communication and collaboration systems

acceptance criteria

Detailed explanation

Remote work is an employment or service arrangement in which work is performed outside a traditional shared workplace and coordinated through agreed digital systems, schedules, outputs, and policies. Professional remote work is measured by useful outcomes, not online activity. A strong system makes expectations visible and preserves evidence from first contact through final handover.

  • Position clearly: name the client, problem, deliverable, result, and limits.
  • Prove before promising: use relevant samples, case studies, tests, or references you have permission to share.
  • Agree in writing: confirm scope, price, currency, timing, responsibilities, revisions, rights, payment, and acceptance.
  • Deliver visibly: plan milestones, report early, protect information, check quality, and record decisions.

Step-by-step professional method

  1. Choose service: define the goal, person responsible, evidence, constraints, and success condition.
  2. Prove ability: organize the work, tools, information, access, schedule, and safeguards.
  3. Agree terms: execute carefully, communicate progress, and document decisions or changes.
  4. Deliver reliably: check acceptance, hand over securely, record payment, request feedback, and improve.

Worked client example

A learner inventories skills already used in school, church, business, or community work, identifies one client problem, creates a sample solution, and tests whether real buyers request that result.

Why it works: the example replaces vague promises with evidence, written boundaries, responsible communication, secure behavior, and measurable follow-through.

Professional checklist

  • Verify the client, platform, message, link, file, payment status, and written agreement.
  • Confirm scope, exclusions, deliverables, acceptance criteria, deadlines, availability, and revision limits.
  • Protect accounts with unique passwords, multi-factor authentication, updates, backups, and least access.
  • Keep a decision log, versions, time or milestone evidence, invoices, receipts, and tax-ready records.
  • Never claim skills, results, testimonials, certifications, or work that you cannot prove.
